responsibility.value: For authenticated requests, eagerly resolves and caches the current store id on ICurrentActor early in the pipeline, so later code paths (including EF Core's per-request tenant query filter) get a warm value instead of resolving it lazily on first use.

Owns: Pre-warming actor.GetCurrentStoreIdAsync() once per authenticated request
Swallowing StoreNotResolvedException so non-store roles (students, instructors) pass through unaffected
doesNotOwn: Actual tenant data filtering — that is enforced by ENoteContext's global query filters (OnModelCreating), which call the same ICurrentActor.GetCurrentStoreId() this middleware pre-warms
Authentication itself — this middleware only acts on already-authenticated requests

collaborators.detail: GetCurrentStoreIdAsync() — the same resolution path EF Core's query filters use synchronously via GetCurrentStoreId()

contracts: A request from a non-store-employee role (no resolvable store) proceeds normally — StoreNotResolvedException is not surfaced as an error.
assumptions: ICurrentActor caches the resolved store id internally (e.g. in a per-request/scoped field) so that this middleware's early resolution is actually reused by ENoteContext's later query-filter calls rather than re-querying. If ICurrentActor is not scoped/cached correctly, this middleware provides no benefit and is purely inert.
This middleware is registered early enough in the pipeline (after authentication, before any DB-touching endpoint code) for the pre-warm to matter.
failureModes: None surfaced to the caller — StoreNotResolvedException is caught and ignored by design.
architecturalNotes: This class does not itself enforce tenant isolation — that lives in eNote.Infrastructure.Data.ENoteContext.OnModelCreating, which reflects over all ITenantScoped entity types and applies a HasQueryFilter scoped to GetStoreId(). This middleware is purely a performance/warm-cache concern; a bug here would affect latency, not correctness. A bug in the ENoteContext filter setup is the actual tenant-isolation risk.
